evidence: Kernel-proved simultaneous guarded elimination of arbitrarily many hidden pairs, plus a hidden-triangle obstruction to state-forgetting.
proved: For every finite graph and palette, a hidden set partitioned into blocks of size at most two with no cross-block hidden edges has connected restriction fibres.

Joint before/after transition guards factor into one condition per hidden block. Shared retained neighbours are permitted and use one common colouring. The factorization alone does not require small blocks.
The factored guarded histories coincide with actual boundary-avoiding Kempe histories for the proved pair-block domain.
Three hidden vertices forming a triangle can already have disconnected fibres: two full colourings project to the same retained state. Restricting abstract steps alone cannot repair that loss.
program_scope: Two 155-vertex exteriors of 162-vertex spheres. The selected partitions hide 53 and 52 vertices with 30 and 29 guards, versus 33 independent hidden vertices previously. Both blocked commands remain rejected; both successful two-switch full reconstructions replay.
negative_controls: Splitting an adjacent hidden pair into distinct blocks rejected
scope: An unbounded family of faithful constrained interfaces, not an ordinary graph reduction or a proved closure law under repeated elimination. The three-vertex obstruction has pendant vertices; no minimal-counterexample geometric obstruction is asserted.
